question.problem: The length of one leg of a right triangle increases at the rate of $3\text{ m/s},$ while the length of the second leg is decreasing at the rate of $2\text{ m/s}.$ How fast is the length of the hypotenuse changing when the length of the increasing leg is $12\text{ m}$ and the length of the decreasing leg is $16\text{ m}?$
question.worked_solution:
We start by drawing a diagram of the problem.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14208490/assets/eee3de464da57671142e2677974b44c63dc2397215ffdd2aa36e2c3d401a647d.png)

In the diagram,

- $x$ is the length of the increasing side,

- $y$ is the length of the decreasing side,

- $z$ is the length of the hypotenuse.

As shown in the diagram, $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ form a right triangle with $z$ as the hypotenuse. We wish to find the rate of change of $z,$ which is $\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}.$ 

We know that $x=12\,\text{m}$ and $y=16\,\text{m}.$ We can find $z$ using the Pythagorean Theorem, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={z}^{2} \\ {12}^{2}+{16}^{2} & ={z}^{2} \\ 400 & ={z}^{2} \\ z & =20\,\text{m}\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that:

- $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=3\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $x=12\,\text{m}$ and $y=16\,\text{m},$

- $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=-2\,\text{m}/\text{s}$  when $x=12\,\text{m}$ and $y=16\,\text{m}.$

Finally, we differentiate both sides of ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}={z}^{2}$ with respect to $t$ and then substitute in the known values, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({z}^{2}) \\ 2x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =2z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} \\ 2(12)(3)+2(16)(-2) & =2(20)\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} \\ 8 & =40\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{8}{40} \\ \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the length of the hypotenuse is changing at a rate of $\frac{1}{5}\,\text{m}/\text{s}.$
